- `.dark` block defines dark-mode CSS variables (lines 32-52)
- `body` correctly uses `var(--background)` and `var(--foreground)` (lines 54-58)

#### 4. layout.tsx has `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`
**File:** `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\app\layout.tsx` (line 27)
This is correct and necessary for next-themes to inject the dark class without React hydration errors.

#### 5. THE BUG: Missing `@custom-variant dark` in Tailwind CSS v4
**File:** `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\app\globals.css`

In Tailwind CSS v4 (v4.3.3 in this project), the `dark:` variant defaults to the **`prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query**. It does NOT look for the `.dark` class on a parent element. To make Tailwind's `dark:` variant class-based (matching next-themes' `attribute="class"`), you **must** add this to your CSS:

```css
@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));
```

This directive is **completely absent** from the project. Without it, all `dark:` utility classes across the entire application (`dark:bg-gray-900`, `dark:text-white`, `dark:border-gray-700`, etc.) respond **only** to the OS/browser `prefers-color-scheme` media query, not the `.dark` class toggled by next-themes.

### What the user experiences

1. User selects "Light mode" in the toggle
2. next-themes removes the `.dark` class from `<html>`
3. **CSS custom properties switch to light correctly** (because they are scoped to `.dark {}` vs `:root {}`)
4. **BUT** all `dark:` Tailwind utility classes across every component continue to apply if the OS is in dark mode, because they still respond to `prefers-color-scheme: dark` -- they ignore the `.dark` class entirely
5. Result: a visual **inconsistency** -- some elements appear light (CSS-var-based), while most elements (all the Tailwind `dark:` classes) remain dark

### The Fix

Add the `@custom-variant` directive to `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\app\globals.css`, at the top (after the existing `@import "tailwindcss"` line):

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));

@theme inline {
  /* ... existing theme block ... */
}
```

This single line makes Tailwind v4's `dark:` variant respond to the `.dark` class on any ancestor element, which is exactly what next-themes' `attribute="class"` produces.

### Additional Note

The `next.config.ts` file is essentially empty (no configuration options set). This is not related to the bug but worth noting. The `tailwind.config` file does not exist, which is normal for Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first configuration).

### Summary Table

| Component | Status | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| ThemeProvider config (`attribute="class"`) | Correct | None |
| ThemeToggle component | Correct | None |
| `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` | Correct | None |
| CSS custom variables (light/dark) | Correct | None |
| `body` background/color using vars | Correct | None |
| **`@custom-variant dark` directive** | **MISSING** | **Tailwind v4 `dark:` utilities use OS media query, not `.dark` class** |
</task_result>

# Frontend Design Audit Report

## Summary

This is a Tailwind CSS v4 + Next.js 16 + next-themes based school management dashboard. The design system is built on CSS custom properties with `.dark` class-based dark mode. Overall the codebase is reasonably well-structured, but there are several notable issues across the files.

---

## 1. `globals.css` — CSS Variables & Theme Setup

**File:** `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\app\globals.css`

| Line(s) | Issue | Severity |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **3-8** | The `@theme inline` block maps `--color-background` and `--color-foreground` from the CSS custom properties, but does **not** map the other 18+ variables (`--card`, `--primary`, `--border`, `--muted`, `--accent`, etc.) into the Tailwind v4 theme. This means Tailwind utility classes like `bg-card`, `text-primary`, `border-border`, `bg-muted` etc. are **not available** — the only theme-aware Tailwind utilities are `bg-background` and `text-foreground`. Every other color in the codebase must use arbitrary Tailwind values or hardcoded color classes. This is a significant design system gap. | High |
| **32** | The `.dark` class selector only works with `class` strategy in `next-themes`. This is correct, but the `@theme inline` block should be the canonical source of truth — right now the variables in `:root` / `.dark` and the `@theme inline` are disconnected. Any new CSS variable added to `:root`/`.dark` will need manual wiring in the `@theme inline` block. This is fragile. | Medium |
| **54-58** | The `body` rule sets `background-color` and `color` from variables, which is redundant with Tailwind v4's theming. It also doesn't set `min-height` or layout defaults, leaving that to individual page layouts. | Low |
| **60-76** | The `@keyframes modalIn` and `modal-content`/`modal-overlay` utility classes use raw CSS. These don't follow the Tailwind animation pattern and won't be tree-shaken. They're also not available as Tailwind utilities (`animate-modalIn` won't work). | Low |
| **(missing)** | No `scrollbar` styling for dark mode. WebKit browsers show a bright scrollbar in dark mode which is a common dark-mode UX issue. | Medium |

---

## 2. `sidebar.tsx` — Sidebar Design

**File:** `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\components\layout\sidebar.tsx`

| **33** | `icon: any` — The icon type is `any` instead of `LucideIcon` or `React.ComponentType`. This is a TypeScript anti-pattern, not strictly a design issue, but it can lead to runtime crashes with incorrect icon components. | Low |
| **83** | Sidebar background is `bg-white dark:bg-gray-900`. This is a **hardcoded color** that doesn't use the `--card` or `--background` CSS variable. In `globals.css`, `--background` in dark mode is `#0a0a0a`, but the sidebar uses `gray-900` (`#111827`). This means the sidebar is visibly lighter than the main content area in dark mode. | Medium |

The gradient is subtle (600->700 is ~10% lightness difference) but it means buttons look glossy/gradient while everything else is flat. This is a **visual inconsistency** — cards, sidebar, header are all flat, but buttons have gradients. | Medium |
| **18** | Primary button has `shadow-lg shadow-blue-500/25` — a colored box shadow. This is a modern design pattern but it's the **only component** that uses colored shadows. Cards have `shadow-sm`, sidebar has none. This makes buttons look like they belong to a different design language. | Medium |
| **20** | Danger variant also uses gradient + colored shadow (`from-red-500 to-red-600 shadow-red-500/25`). Same inconsistency issue as primary. | Medium |
| **16** | `dark:focus:ring-offset-gray-900` — this is hardcoded to match `--background: #0a0a0a` in dark mode. If the background color changes, the focus ring offset will look wrong. Should use a CSS variable. | Low |
| **29** | Disabled/loading state uses `opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed`. The `opacity-50` applies to the **entire button** including text, making it hard to read. A better pattern is `opacity-60` or `pointer-events-none` with a specific disabled background color. | Low |
| **24-26** | Size classes: `sm` is `px-3 py-1.5`, `md` is `px-4 py-2`, `lg` is `px-6 py-3`. The padding ratio is inconsistent: sm=2.25:1, md=2:1, lg=2:1. The `sm` is proportionally wider. Minor but noticeable in tight layouts. | Low |
| **(missing)** | No `outline` variant. Common in design systems for tertiary actions. Only `primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `ghost` are available. | Info |
| **(missing)** | No `icon` or `icon-only` size variant. Buttons with only icons (like the menu button in header) have to override sizes manually. | Info |

---

## 7. `data-table.tsx` — Table Design

**File:** `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\frontend\src\components\ui\data-table.tsx`

| Line(s) | Issue | Severity |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **50** | Table header uses `bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-800/50` — hardcoded. The 50% opacity in dark mode is a nice touch for hierarchy, but it's hardcoded rather than using a variable. | Low |
| **54** | Header text is `text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400` — hardcoded. | Low |
| **79** | Row uses `even:bg-gray-50 dark:even:bg-gray-800/50` — zebra striping with hardcoded colors. | Low |
| **79** | Row hover is `hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700/50` — this **conflicts** with the even-row stripe. On even rows in dark mode, the base is `gray-800/50` and hover goes to `gray-700/50` — the difference is very subtle (only ~3% lightness). On odd rows, hover goes from transparent to `gray-700/50` which is more noticeable. The hover feedback is inconsistent between odd and even rows. | Medium |
| **47** | `overflow-x-auto rounded-xl` wraps the table, but the `<table>` has `w-full` and no `min-w-*`. On very narrow screens, the table will scroll but the rounded corners of the container won't clip the table corners (tables don't respect `overflow: hidden` parent radius in all browsers). | Low |
| **35** | Loading spinner uses `border-b-2 border-blue-600 dark:border-blue-400` — hardcoded blue. Should use `--primary`. | Low |
| **(missing)** | No pagination component. The table renders all data at once. For large datasets this will cause performance issues. | High |
| **(missing)** | No row selection capability (checkboxes). Many CRUD dashboards need bulk actions (delete selected, export selected). | Info |
| **(missing)** | No `aria-sort` on sortable columns. Screen readers can't determine sort state. | Low |
| **(missing)** | No `role="table"` or `scope="col"` on `<th>` elements. While `<table>` is semantic, explicit ARIA helps complex tables. | Low |
| **(missing)** | Empty state (line 42) is plain text. Should have an illustration or icon for better UX, matching the loading state which has a spinner. | Low |

---

## Cross-Cutting Issues

### 1. Inconsistent Color Strategy (HIGH)
The CSS variable system in `globals.css` defines 18+ semantic tokens (`--card`, `--primary`, `--border`, `--muted`, `--accent`, etc.), but the `@theme inline` block only maps 2 of them (`--background`, `--foreground`). As a result, **every component uses hardcoded Tailwind color classes** (`bg-white`, `dark:bg-gray-800`, `text-blue-600`, `border-gray-200`, etc.) instead of theme tokens. The semantic variables are effectively dead code — they exist but nothing references them.

**Affected files:** Every file listed above.

### 2. Inconsistent Dark Mode Colors (MEDIUM)
Different components use different dark-mode background values:
- Sidebar: `dark:bg-gray-900` (#111827)
- Header: `dark:bg-gray-900` (#111827)
- Card: `dark:bg-gray-800` (#1f2937)
- Main content: `dark:bg-gray-900` (#111827)
- Table header: `dark:bg-gray-800/50`
- Search results dropdown: `dark:bg-gray-800`

The CSS variable `--background` is `#0a0a0a` in dark mode, but no component uses it. The result is that dark mode backgrounds are **lighter** than what the design system intends, and there's no visual hierarchy between surfaces (sidebar, header, cards all blend together).

### 3. No `bg-background` or `bg-card` Usage (MEDIUM)
Despite defining CSS variables for `--background` and `--card`, the codebase uses `bg-white dark:bg-gray-*` everywhere. This means:
- Theme customization via CSS variables has no effect
- The `@theme inline` mapping is wasted
- If you want to change the primary color, you'd need to update 30+ hardcoded `blue-*` references

### 4. Missing Focus Ring Consistency (LOW)
Some interactive elements have focus rings (buttons via `focus:ring-2`), but sidebar links, search results, and table sort buttons do not. This creates an inconsistent keyboard navigation experience.

### 5. No Transition on Layout (LOW)
The dashboard layout has `transition-colors duration-200` on the main container (line 102), which is good for theme switching. But the sidebar and header don't have this transition, so theme changes flash the sidebar/header instantly while the main content fades.

---

## Priority Recommendations

1. **[HIGH]** Complete the `@theme inline` block in `globals.css` to map all CSS variables (`--card`, `--primary`, `--border`, etc.) into Tailwind v4 tokens. Then replace all hardcoded color classes with theme-aware utilities.

2. **[HIGH]** Add pagination to `DataTable` — rendering unbounded data will cause performance problems.

3. **[HIGH]** Fix the loading skeleton mismatch in `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` line 65 — change `bg-gray-900` to `bg-white dark:bg-gray-900` or better, `bg-card`.

4. **[MEDIUM]** Standardize dark mode surface colors using the CSS variable hierarchy: `--background` < `--card` < `--popover` for visual layering.

5. **[MEDIUM]** Make sidebar active state detection use `startsWith` instead of exact match for nested routes.

6. **[MEDIUM]** Remove gradients and colored shadows from `Button` to match the flat design language of the rest of the UI, or add them consistently everywhere.

7. **[MEDIUM]** Add keyboard accessibility to search results dropdown (`role="listbox"`, `role="option"`, `tabIndex`, `onKeyDown`).

# Backend Controller Audit Report

## Global Configuration Finding

**File**: `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\backend\src\common\pipes\validation.pipe.ts`

The global `AppValidationPipe` is configured with:
```typescript
whitelist: true,
forbidNonWhitelisted: true,
transform: true,

```

This is the root cause of several categories of 400 errors. `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` means **any unknown property in the body OR query string will return a 400**.

## ISSUE #1 (CRITICAL) -- `PaginationQueryDto` `@IsIn` case sensitivity on `sortOrder`

**File**: `E:\ReFactory\BSofts-School\backend\src\common\dto\pagination.dto.ts` (line 47)
```typescript
@IsOptional()
@IsString()
@IsIn(['asc', 'desc'])
sortOrder?: 'asc' | 'desc' = 'asc';
```

**Impact**: This affects ALL 19 paginated controllers. If the frontend sends `?sortOrder=ASC` (uppercase) or `?sortOrder=Descending`, it returns **400 Bad Request** because `@IsIn` uses strict equality. Also, sending `?sortOrder=` (empty string) will fail because `@IsOptional()` only skips validation for `undefined`/`null`, not empty strings.

**Affected controllers**: All controllers except `reports.controller.ts`.

---

## ISSUE #2 (CRITICAL) -- `@IsEnum` on query parameters is case-sensitive

Multiple query DTOs use `@IsEnum([...])` on query parameters. Enum values are uppercase (e.g., `QUIZ`, `MALE`, `PENDING`), but the frontend might send lowercase or mixed-case values, causing **400 errors**.

| DTO | Field | Enum Values | File |
|-----|-------|------------|------|
| `QueryExamDto` | `type` | `QUIZ, MIDTERM, FINAL...` | `exams/dto/exam.dto.ts:120` |

| `QueryStudentPaymentDto` | `status` | `PENDING, PAID, PARTIAL...` | `student-payments/dto/student-payment.dto.ts:92` |
| `QueryStudentPaymentDto` | `method` | `CASH, CHECK, CARD...` | `student-payments/dto/student-payment.dto.ts:97` |
| `QueryNotificationDto` | `type` | `INFO, WARNING, SUCCESS...` | `notifications/dto/notification.dto.ts:36` |
| `QueryConversationDto` | `type` | `DIRECT, GROUP, ANNOUNCEMENT` | `conversations/dto/conversation.dto.ts:22` |
| `QueryTransactionDto` | `type` | `INCOME, EXPENSE, TRANSFER...` | `financial-transactions/dto/financial-transaction.dto.ts:52` |
| `QueryCaisseDto` | `type` | `MAIN, PETTY_CASH, BANK...` | `caisses/dto/caisse.dto.ts:58` |

**Affected controllers**: `exams`, `rooms`, `student-payments`, `notifications`, `conversations`, `financial-transactions`, `caisses`.

Because `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` is set globally, **any query parameter not declared in the DTO will return 400**. This is dangerous because:

- Frontend developers often send extra query params for debugging
- Analytics/tracking params (like `?utm_source=...`) would break requests
- Browser extensions may inject extra query params

For example, `GET /api/students?page=1&foo=bar` would return **400** because `QueryStudentDto` has no `foo` property.

**Affected controllers**: All controllers that accept `@Query()` DTOs (all except `reports.controller.ts`).

```typescript
  @IsString()
  sessionId: string;

  attendances: Array<{

  @IsOptional()

}
```

**Problems**:

## ANALYSIS RESULTS

### 1. Landing Page
- Plans are **hardcoded** (Free 0, Basic 4,900, Premium 19,900) — should fetch from `/api/saas-plans`
- No mobile hamburger menu
- No language selector or theme toggle in navbar

### 2. Auth Pages
- Both login and register already have a logo link back to `/` ✅
- Register has **no plan selection** — users register without choosing a subscription
- Auth layout has hardcoded English text, no i18n

### 3. SaaS Admin
- Admin pages exist (plans, tenants, subscriptions, permissions) but:
  - **No client-side route guard** — any authenticated user can access `/admin/*`
  - Subscriptions page is read-only (no create/edit/cancel)
  - Tenants page has no create functionality
  - Permissions page has no role CRUD
  - No "Modules" or "Functions" management views

### 4. Forms vs Schema — Missing Fields

| Form | Missing Fields | Extra/Bogus Fields |
|------|---------------|-------------------|
| Student | `bio` | `email` (cross-model) |
| Teacher | `bio` | `specialization` labeled as "Description" |
| Employee | `bio`, `address` | — |
| Holiday | `description` | Checkbox labeled with wrong key |
| Exam | `description`, `isOnline`, `antiCheat`, `maxAttempts` | — |
| Payment | `parentId` (no UI), `dueDate`, `currency` | `paymentDate` sent instead of `paidAt` |
| Parent | Complete ✅ | — |
| Room | Complete ✅ | — |
| Class | — | `description` (not in schema) |

### 5. Modals
- All use `size="lg"` — no `xl` used
- No section groupings (all flat)
- No wizard pattern for complex forms

---

## PROPOSED PLAN

### Phase 1: Landing Page & Auth (HIGH priority)
1. Fetch plans from API (`GET /api/landing/plans`) instead of hardcoded
2. Add mobile hamburger menu to landing navbar
3. Add language selector + theme toggle to landing navbar
4. Add plan selection step to register page
5. Add i18n to auth layout branding text

### Phase 2: Route Protection & SaaS Admin (HIGH priority)
6. Add client-side Root role guard in dashboard layout
7. Add "Modules" management view (CRUD for SaaSModule)
8. Enhance subscriptions page with create/edit/cancel
9. Enhance tenants page with create functionality
10. Add role CRUD to permissions page

### Phase 3: Form Improvements (MEDIUM priority)
11. Add missing fields to all forms (bio, address, description, etc.)
12. Fix mislabeled fields (specialization, checkbox label)
13. Fix payment form (parentId UI, dueDate, currency)
14. Remove bogus fields (Class description)
15. Add `isActive` toggle to relevant forms

### Phase 4: Modal & UX Improvements (MEDIUM priority)
16. Upgrade modals to `size="xl"` for forms
17. Add section groupings (Personal Info, Contact, Academic, etc.)
18. Add wizard pattern for Exam and Payment forms (multi-step)

These are grouped by domain priority:

#### HIGH PRIORITY -- Business-critical missing APIs

| Model | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| **`ClassLevel`** | Reference data needed for class creation. Classes reference `classLevelId` but there is no way to manage class levels via API. |
| **`ClassSchedule`** | Weekly timetables for classes. Rooms, teachers, and matieres all reference through this. No scheduling API exists. |
| **`TeacherContract`** | Teachers have contracts but no CRUD for them. Teacher payments reference `contractId` but contracts cannot be managed. |
| **`EmployeeContract`** | Same gap as TeacherContract for employees. |
| **`ExamQuestion`** | Exams have questions but there is no way to create/manage them via API. |
| **`ExamSubmission`** | Student exam submissions have no API -- online exams are unusable. |
| **`ExamAnswer`** | Individual answers to exam questions have no API. |
| **`Bulletin`** | Report cards / bulletins have no generation or retrieval API. |
| **`PaymentPlan`** | Payment plans exist in schema but cannot be created or managed. StudentPayments reference `planId`. |
| **`StudentClassAssignment`** | No API to assign students to classes per academic year. Critical for enrollment. |
| **`StudentParent`** | No API to link parents to students. The parent-student relationship is unmanageable. |
| **`TeacherMatiere`** | No API to assign teachers to subjects (matieres). |

#### MEDIUM PRIORITY -- Configuration & settings gaps

| Model | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| **`TenantSettings`** | Currency, language, theme, timezone per tenant -- no settings API. |
| **`EstablishmentConfig`** | Establishment-level configuration (academic year start, anti-cheat flags) -- no API. |
| **`GradingConfig`** | Grading scales, pass thresholds -- no API to configure. |
| **`SmtpConfig`** | Email server configuration -- no API. |
| **`NotificationConfig`** | Notification preferences per establishment -- no API. |
| **`PaymentConfig`** | Payment gateway settings (Stripe, PayPal) -- no API. |

#### LOWER PRIORITY -- Junction/auxiliary tables

| Model | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| **`SaaSPlanModule`** | Junction table, though partially covered via `saas-plans/:id/modules` endpoint. |
| **`SaaSPlanFeature`** | Plan features cannot be managed via dedicated API. |
| **`TenantPlanFeatureOverride`** | Per-tenant feature overrides have no API. |
| **`ClassModuleAssignment`** | No API to assign academic modules to classes. |
| **`RoomEquipment`** | Room equipment tracking has no API. |
| **`ConversationParticipant`** | Managed implicitly through conversations service but no dedicated endpoints. |
| **`NotificationTemplate`** | Notification templates cannot be managed via API. |
| **`ProfitLoss`** | Profit/loss reports have no dedicated CRUD API. |
| **`GraduationConfig`** | Graduation/promotion rules have no API. |
| **`GraduationRecord`** | Student promotion records have no API. |

### Additional Observations

1. **`reports.controller.ts`** has only a single `POST /reports/generate` endpoint -- no GET endpoints to retrieve previously generated reports.
2. **`landing.controller.ts`** is a public-facing controller that reads from `SaaSPlan` and `SaaSModule` but is not tied to a Prisma model of its own.
3. **`financial-transactions`** has no `PUT` or `DELETE` endpoints -- transactions are immutable (by design, likely).
4. The **`bulletin`**, **`graduation`**, and **`exam`** subsystems are only partially built -- the core models exist but the full question/submission/answer pipeline and the bulletin generation pipeline have no API layer at all.

| Gap | Severity | Details |
|-----|----------|---------|
| **PermissionsGuard not used on most controllers** | HIGH | Only 2 out of ~30 controllers use `PermissionsGuard` (`reports`, `audit-logs`). All others use only `RolesGuard`. This means a TEACHER with `@Permissions('payments:create')` on a route would still be blocked by `RolesGuard` checking role codes, but the granular permission system (161 permissions) is largely unused at the guard level. |
| **RolesGuard uses hardcoded role codes** | MEDIUM | Controllers use `@Roles('ROOT', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'ADMIN')` etc. These are hardcoded strings, not derived from the database. The `RolesGuard` checks `user.roles[].role.code` against these hardcoded values. |
| **No global PermissionsGuard** | HIGH | `PermissionsGuard` is not registered as a global guard (`APP_GUARD`). It must be manually applied per-controller. Currently most controllers only have `RolesGuard`. |
| **ROOT role not in Role table** | LOW | `ROOT` is referenced in some `@Roles()` decorators (e.g., `establishments.controller.ts:45,63`) but is not in the seed roles. ROOT is handled via the `isRoot` boolean on User, bypassing both guards. |
| **Inconsistent guard combinations** | MEDIUM | Some controllers use `JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard`, others use `JwtAuthGuard + PermissionsGuard`, and some use only `JwtAuthGuard`. There's no consistent pattern. |

| **PermissionsGuard requires establishmentId** | MEDIUM | If `request.establishmentId` is null (ROOT user or missing header), the guard throws `ForbiddenException`. ROOT users bypass this, but other users without an establishment context would be blocked. |
| **No data scoping by establishment in services** | HIGH | Services do not filter queries by `establishmentId` from the JWT/auth context. Data is scoped only if the frontend sends the correct `establishmentId` in the request body/query/header. This means a user from Establishment A could access Establishment B data if they craft the right request. |
| **JWT token does not include permissions** | MEDIUM | The JWT payload only has `sub`, `email`, `username`. Permissions are only available after querying the DB in `PermissionsGuard`. This means every permission-checking request requires a DB query. |

| **No permission-based route guards** | CRITICAL | No frontend component checks if the user has a specific permission before rendering a page. All dashboard pages are accessible to all authenticated users. |
| **No permission-based UI filtering** | CRITICAL | No buttons, links, or UI elements are hidden based on user permissions. A TEACHER can see "Delete" buttons on all pages. |
| **Sidebar shows all items to all users** | HIGH | The sidebar renders the same navigation items for all authenticated users (except root admin section). A TEACHER sees Payments, Settings, Reports, etc. in the sidebar. |
| **No permissions store/hook** | HIGH | There is no `usePermissions()` hook, no `permissions-store.ts`, and the auth store does not fetch or store permission codes. |
| **establishmentId not sent in API requests** | HIGH | The frontend never sends the `x-establishment-id` header. The `EstablishmentContextMiddleware` extracts it, but it's never provided. This means `request.establishmentId` is always null for frontend-originated requests, which would cause `PermissionsGuard` to fail. |
| **establishmentId is hardcoded from first userRole** | MEDIUM | `auth-store.ts:70` extracts `establishmentId` from `userRoles[0]`. If a user has roles in multiple establishments, only the first is used. No multi-establishment switching UI exists. |
| **No 403 (Forbidden) handling** | MEDIUM | The API response interceptor only handles 401. There's no handling for 403 Forbidden responses, which would be thrown by guards. |
| **Admin page not permission-gated properly** | MEDIUM | The admin permissions page is only gated by `isRoot` check in the layout. It doesn't check if the user has `roles:create` or `permissions:manage` permissions. |

---

## 4. WHAT NEEDS TO BE BUILT

### 4.1 Backend -- Priority 1 (Security-Critical)

1. **Register `PermissionsGuard` as a global guard** -- In `main.ts` or `app.module.ts`, register it via `APP_GUARD` token so all endpoints are checked by default. This makes the default "guarded" and controllers only need to opt out with `@Public()`.

2. **Add establishment data scoping to all services** -- Every service method that queries data by establishment must filter by the establishment ID from the auth context (not from the request body). Create a utility/middleware that enforces `establishmentId` filtering at the service or Prisma level.

3. **Send establishmentId from frontend** -- Add `x-establishment-id` header to the Axios interceptor in `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, reading from the auth store's `user.establishmentId`.

4. **Add permission checks to unprotected controllers** -- Apply `@Permissions()` decorators to `notifications`, `conversations`, and `messages` controllers.

### 4.2 Backend -- Priority 2 (Architecture)

5. **Include permissions in JWT payload or create a fast cache** -- Either embed permission codes in the JWT (updated on role change) or create a Redis/in-memory cache for permission lookups to avoid DB queries on every request.

6. **Standardize guard usage** -- Decide on a single pattern: either use `PermissionsGuard` everywhere (granular) or `RolesGuard` everywhere (coarse). The current mix is inconsistent.

7. **Add role-based data filtering** -- For example, a TEACHER should only see their own students' grades; a PARENT should only see their own children's data. This needs to be enforced in service methods, not just at the route level.

8. **Remove hardcoded `ROOT` from `@Roles()` decorators** -- `ROOT` is handled by `isRoot` bypass in guards, so referencing it in `@Roles('ROOT')` is misleading and has no effect.

### 4.3 Frontend -- Priority 1 (Security-Critical)

9. **Create a permissions hook/store** -- Build `usePermissions()` or add permissions to the auth store. Fetch permission codes from the profile endpoint or a new dedicated endpoint, and store them client-side.

10. **Build permission-based route guards** -- Create a `<ProtectedRoute requiredPermission="students:create">` wrapper component or Next.js middleware that checks permissions before rendering pages.

11. **Filter sidebar by permissions** -- Modify `sidebar.tsx` to only show navigation items the user has permission for (e.g., if no `payments:list` permission, hide the Payments menu item).

12. **Hide/show UI actions by permissions** -- Create a `<Can permission="students:delete">` component or `useCan()` hook that conditionally renders buttons, links, and forms based on the user's permissions.

### 4.4 Frontend -- Priority 2 (UX & Multi-Establishment)

13. **Multi-establishment selector** -- If a user has roles in multiple establishments, provide a UI to switch between them (and update the `x-establishment-id` header accordingly).

14. **403 error handling** -- Add a global handler for 403 responses that shows an "Access Denied" message or redirects appropriately.

15. **Role-based welcome/dashboard content** -- Show different dashboard widgets/data based on the user's role (e.g., teachers see their schedule, students see their grades, parents see their children's info).

---

## 5. SUMMARY TABLE

| Area | What Exists | What's Missing |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| **JWT Auth** | Full login/register/refresh flow, JWT strategy, token management | No token rotation on suspicious activity, no rate limiting |
| **Guards** | JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard, PermissionsGuard all implemented | PermissionsGuard used on only 2/30+ controllers; no global guard |
| **Decorators** | @Public, @Roles, @Permissions, @CurrentUser, @TenantId, @EstablishmentId | None missing, but underutilized |
| **RBAC Data Model** | Full Role/Permission/UserRoleAssignment schema with 6 roles + 161 permissions | No ROOT role in DB (handled via boolean) |
| **Middleware** | Subscription + EstablishmentContext middleware globally applied | Frontend never sends establishment context header |
| **Frontend Auth** | Login/register, token storage, profile loading | No permissions fetched or stored |
| **Frontend Route Protection** | Admin routes gated by isRoot only | No permission-based route guards |
| **Frontend UI Filtering** | Root admin nav hidden for non-root users | No permission-based menu/button filtering |
| **Data Scoping** | Establishment ID extracted from request | Not enforced in service queries -- data leak risk |

All complete. **Frontend + Backend compile clean (0 errors).** Here's what was done:

---

## Summary of Everything

### Critical Bugs Fixed
- **Landing page plans**: Changed `fetch('/api/landing/plans')` → `api.get('/landing/plans')` (was hitting non-existent Next.js route)
- **Register page plans**: Fixed response format handling (`Array.isArray(data) ? data : data.data`)
- **Auth layout**: Reverted to server component to prevent SSR 404

### 1. Landing Page (Complete Rewrite)
- **Dynamic stats**: Fetches from `GET /api/landing/stats` (students, teachers, exams, uptime)
- **Smooth scroll**: `scroll-behavior: smooth` on root
- **Scroll animations**: IntersectionObserver-based fade-in-up on all sections
- **"How it Works"**: 3-step section (Sign Up → Configure → Manage)
- **FAQ accordion**: 5 questions with toggle
- **Proper footer**: 4-column layout (Product, Support, Legal, Company) with social icons
- **Language selector**: Extracted into reusable component (no more duplication)

### 2. Reusable Form System
- **`FormModal`**: Wraps Modal + form + error banner + cancel/submit buttons
- **`FormSection`**: Bordered section with title for field grouping
- **`useFormState` hook**: Manages formData, isLoading, error state
- **`usePagination` hook**: Generic pagination for any array
- All 6 inline forms migrated to use FormModal/FormSection

### 3. RBAC Permission System
- **`permissions-store.ts`**: Zustand store fetching 161 permissions from API
- **`Can` component**: `<Can permission="students:create">` hides content
- **`useCan` hook**: Imperative permission check
- **Sidebar filtering**: Only shows nav items user has permission for
- **Route guards**: Dashboard layout redirects if user lacks route permission
- **Button visibility**: Add/Edit/Delete buttons wrapped with `<Can>`

### 4. Dashboard Completeness
- **Pagination**: Added to all 8 list pages (students, teachers, parents, employees, rooms, schedule, holidays, exams)
- **Payments**: Added Edit + Delete with ConfirmDialog
- **Attendance**: Added Delete with ConfirmDialog
- **View buttons**: Wired up on students, teachers, parents, employees, rooms (detail modal)

### 5. Backend APIs Created (5 new modules)
- **ClassLevels**: Full CRUD (critical for class creation)
- **PaymentPlans**: Full CRUD with establishmentId filtering
- **TeacherContracts**: Full CRUD with teacher join
- **EmployeeContracts**: Full CRUD with employee join
- **Bulletins**: Full CRUD with unique constraint check

### 6. i18n (All 3 locales)
- Added 50+ new translation keys (stats, howItWorks, FAQ, modules, nav, pages)
- Fixed all hardcoded English in admin pages (permissions, tenants, subscriptions, plans, modules)
- All dashboard pages fully internationalized

# Premium 3D Website

## Overview

This skill provides architectural guidelines and code patterns for developing premium, high-end 3D websites. It targets developers looking to implement advanced WebGL visual effects, custom shader pipelines, interactive physics elements, and immersive page transitions while maintaining high performance.

## When to Use This Skill

- Use when designing premium or award-winning creative websites with 3D elements.
- Use when integrating Three.js, React Three Fiber (R3F), or Spline with custom shaders (GLSL).
- Use when implementing post-processing effects like bloom, depth-of-field, or custom film grain.
- Use when designing interactive preloaders and high-performance asset loading strategies.
- Use when optimizing complex 3D scenes for mobile responsiveness and performance.

## How It Works

### Step 1: Establish the Render Loop and Scene Architecture
Setting up a robust WebGL context with proper resize handling and performance-friendly pixel ratios is crucial. Keep pixel ratios capped at a maximum of 2 to avoid rendering too many pixels on high-DPI screens.

### Step 2: Implement Shader Effects and Post-Processing
Incorporate post-processing pipelines (using `EffectComposer` or `@react-three/postprocessing`) to add bloom, chromatic aberration, depth of field, or film grain. Keep pass counts low and combine custom fragment shaders to minimize draw calls.

### Step 3: Integrate Interactive Physics and Motion
Utilize physics frameworks (such as Cannon.js or Rapier) or procedural spring animations to make 3D objects react to mouse hover, drag, and click inputs with organic feedback.

### Step 4: Asset Pipeline and Preloader
Optimize 3D models (using Draco compression) and load them using custom loading managers. Render interactive preloaders to entertain users while heavy assets are fetched in the background.

## Examples

### Example 1: Custom Post-processing in React Three Fiber (R3F)

import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { EffectComposer, Bloom, DepthOfField, Vignette } from '@react-three/postprocessing';

export default function PremiumComposer() {
  return (
    <Canvas dpr={[1, 2]} gl={{ powerPreference: "high-performance", antialias: false }}>
      <ambientLight intensity={0.5} />
      <mesh>
        <boxGeometry />
        <meshStandardMaterial emissive="orange" emissiveIntensity={2.0} />
      </mesh>
      
      <EffectComposer disableNormalPass>
        <DepthOfField focusDistance={0} focalLength={0.02} bokehScale={2} height={480} />
        <Bloom luminanceThreshold={0.3} luminanceSmoothing={0.9} height={300} />
        <Vignette eskil={false} offset={0.1} darkness={1.1} />
      </EffectComposer>
    </Canvas>
  );
}

### Example 2: Custom GLSL Shader Material for Liquid/Wavy Effects

import * as THREE from 'three';

const CustomWavyMaterial = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  vertexShader: `
    varying vec2 vUv;
    uniform float uTime;
    void main() {
      vUv = uv;
      vec3 pos = position;
      pos.z += sin(pos.x * 5.0 + uTime) * 0.1;
      pos.z += cos(pos.y * 5.0 + uTime) * 0.1;
      gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(pos, 1.0);
    }
  `,
  fragmentShader: `
    varying vec2 vUv;
    uniform float uTime;
    uniform vec3 uColor;
    void main() {
      float pulse = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(uTime + vUv.x * 10.0);
      gl_FragColor = vec4(uColor * pulse, 1.0);
    }
  `,
  uniforms: {
    uTime: { value: 0.0 },
    uColor: { value: new THREE.Color('#3b82f6') }
  }
});

## Best Practices

- Set `dpr={[1, 2]}` to restrict the device pixel ratio to a maximum of 2.
- Disable antialiasing on the WebGLRenderer when post-processing is active to prevent double-aliasing performance penalties.
- Bake ambient occlusion, lighting, and shadows into textures using Blender or other 3D software instead of using dynamic lights and real-time shadows.
- Use instance rendering (`THREE.InstancedMesh` or R3F `<Instances>`) for scenes containing multiple identical meshes.
- Avoid using uncompressed GLTF/OBJ models. Always compress models using Draco or Meshopt.
- Avoid real-time shadow maps (such as `THREE.DirectionalLightShadow`) on mobile or low-end devices due to the heavy performance overhead.

## Limitations

- This skill does not replace environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.
- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, or safety boundaries are missing.
- Complex shader mathematics and advanced physics simulation bounds require manual testing across different device chipsets.

## Security & Safety Notes

- Verify that external 3D model URLs (loaded via `GLTFLoader`) are hosted on trusted, secure CDNs (HTTPS).
- Do not execute arbitrary, unvalidated shell scripts or use unpinned NPM packages to optimize assets.

## Common Pitfalls

- **Problem**: Severe lag/framerate drop on mobile or high-DPI (Retina) screens.
  **Solution**: Ensure the pixel ratio is limited to 2 (`renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2))`) and disable unused post-processing passes.
- **Problem**: Long loading times and white screens during initialization.
  **Solution**: Use a loading manager (`THREE.LoadingManager`) and display a responsive, interactive preloader to keep the user engaged.

### When Invoked

### Step 0: Recommend Specialist and Stop
If the issue is specifically about:

### Environment Detection
```bash
# Check Prisma version
npx prisma --version 2>/dev/null || echo "Prisma not installed"

# Check database provider
grep "provider" prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | head -1

# Check for existing migrations
ls -la prisma/migrations/ 2>/dev/null | head -5

# Check Prisma Client generation status
ls -la node_modules/.prisma/client/ 2>/dev/null | head -3
```

### Apply Strategy
1. Identify the Prisma-specific issue category
2. Check for common anti-patterns in schema or queries
3. Apply progressive fixes (minimal -> better -> complete)
4. Validate with Prisma CLI and testing

## Problem Playbooks

### Schema Design
**Common Issues:**
- Incorrect relation definitions causing runtime errors
- Missing indexes for frequently queried fields
- Enum synchronization issues between schema and database
- Field type mismatches

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
# Validate schema
npx prisma validate

# Check for schema drift
npx prisma migrate diff --from-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --to-schema-datasource prisma/schema.prisma

# Format schema
npx prisma format
```

**Prioritized Fixes:**
1. **Minimal**: Fix relation annotations, add missing `@relation` directives
2. **Better**: Add proper indexes with `@@index`, optimize field types
3. **Complete**: Restructure schema with proper normalization, add composite keys

**Best Practices:**
```prisma
// Good: Explicit relations with clear naming
model User {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  email     String   @unique
  posts     Post[]   @relation("UserPosts")
  profile   Profile? @relation("UserProfile")
  
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  
  @@index([email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Post {
  id       String @id @default(cuid())
  title    String
  author   User   @relation("UserPosts", fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId String
  
  @@index([authorId])
  @@map("posts")
}
```

### Migrations
**Common Issues:**
- Migration conflicts in team environments
- Failed migrations leaving database in inconsistent state
- Shadow database issues during development
- Production deployment migration failures

**Prioritized Fixes:**
1. **Minimal**: Reset development database with `prisma migrate reset`
2. **Better**: Manually fix migration SQL, use `prisma migrate resolve`
3. **Complete**: Squash migrations, create baseline for fresh setup

**Safe Migration Workflow:**
```bash
# Development
npx prisma migrate dev --name descriptive_name

# Production (never use migrate dev!)
npx prisma migrate deploy

# If migration fails in production
npx prisma migrate resolve --applied "migration_name"
# or
npx prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back "migration_name"
```

### Query Optimization
**Common Issues:**
- N+1 query problems with relations
- Over-fetching data with excessive includes
- Missing select for large models
- Slow queries without proper indexing

**Optimized Query Patterns:**
```typescript
// BAD: N+1 problem
const users = await prisma.user.findMany();
for (const user of users) {
  const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({ where: { authorId: user.id } });
}

// GOOD: Include relations
const users = await prisma.user.findMany({
  include: { posts: true }
});

// BETTER: Select only needed fields
const users = await prisma.user.findMany({
  select: {
    id: true,
    email: true,
    posts: {
      select: { id: true, title: true }
    }
  }
});

// BEST for complex queries: Use $queryRaw
const result = await prisma.$queryRaw`
  SELECT u.id, u.email, COUNT(p.id) as post_count
  FROM users u
  LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.author_id = u.id
  GROUP BY u.id
`;
```

### Connection Management
**Connection Configuration:**
```typescript
// For serverless (Vercel, AWS Lambda)
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const globalForPrisma = global as unknown as { prisma: PrismaClient };

export const prisma =
  globalForPrisma.prisma ||
  new PrismaClient({
    log: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' ? ['query'] : [],
  });

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma;

// Graceful shutdown
process.on('beforeExit', async () => {
  await prisma.$disconnect();
});
```

```env
# Connection URL with pool settings
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db?connection_limit=5&pool_timeout=10"
```

### Transaction Patterns
**Transaction Patterns:**
```typescript
// Sequential operations (auto-transaction)
const [user, profile] = await prisma.$transaction([
  prisma.user.create({ data: userData }),
  prisma.profile.create({ data: profileData }),
]);

// Interactive transaction with manual control
const result = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  const user = await tx.user.create({ data: userData });
  
  // Business logic validation
  if (user.email.endsWith('@blocked.com')) {
    throw new Error('Email domain blocked');
  }
  
  const profile = await tx.profile.create({
    data: { ...profileData, userId: user.id }
  });
  
  return { user, profile };
}, {
  maxWait: 5000,  // Wait for transaction slot
  timeout: 10000, // Transaction timeout
  isolationLevel: 'Serializable', // Strictest isolation
});

// Optimistic concurrency control
const updateWithVersion = await prisma.post.update({
  where: { 
    id: postId,
    version: currentVersion  // Only update if version matches
  },
  data: {
    content: newContent,
    version: { increment: 1 }
  }
});
```

## Code Review Checklist

### Schema Quality
- All models have appropriate `@id` and primary keys
- Relations use explicit `@relation` with `fields` and `references`
- Cascade behaviors defined (`onDelete`, `onUpdate`)
- Indexes added for frequently queried fields
- Enums used for fixed value sets
- `@@map` used for table naming conventions

### Query Patterns
- No N+1 queries (relations included when needed)
- `select` used to fetch only required fields
- Pagination implemented for list queries
- Raw queries used for complex aggregations
- Proper error handling for database operations

### Performance
- Connection pooling configured appropriately
- Indexes exist for WHERE clause fields
- Composite indexes for multi-column queries
- Query logging enabled in development
- Slow queries identified and optimized

### Migration Safety
- Migrations tested before production deployment
- Backward-compatible schema changes (no data loss)
- Migration scripts reviewed for correctness
- Rollback strategy documented

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid

1. **Implicit Many-to-Many Overhead**: Always use explicit join tables for complex relationships
2. **Over-Including**: Don't include relations you don't need
3. **Ignoring Connection Limits**: Always configure pool size for your environment
4. **Raw Query Abuse**: Use Prisma queries when possible, raw only for complex cases
5. **Migration in Production Dev Mode**: Never use `migrate dev` in production

# Performance Optimization

## Overview

Measure before optimizing. Performance work without measurement is guessing. Profile first, identify the actual bottleneck, fix it, measure again. Optimize only what measurements prove matters.

## Core Web Vitals Targets

| Metric | Good | Needs Improvement | Poor |
|--------|------|-------------------|------|
| **LCP** (Largest Contentful Paint) | <= 2.5s | <= 4.0s | > 4.0s |
| **INP** (Interaction to Next Paint) | <= 200ms | <= 500ms | > 500ms |
| **CLS** (Cumulative Layout Shift) | <= 0.1 | <= 0.25 | > 0.25 |

## The Optimization Workflow

1. MEASURE  -> Establish baseline with real data
2. IDENTIFY -> Find the actual bottleneck (not assumed)
3. FIX      -> Address the specific bottleneck
4. VERIFY   -> Measure again, confirm improvement
5. GUARD    -> Add monitoring or tests to prevent regression

### Where to Start Measuring

Use the symptom to decide what to measure first:
- First page load -> Large bundle? Slow server? Render-blocking resources?
- Interaction feels sluggish -> UI freezes on click? Form input lag? Animation jank?
- Page after navigation -> Data loading? Client rendering?
- Backend / API -> Single endpoint slow? All endpoints slow? Intermittent slowness?

### Step 2: Identify the Bottleneck

**Frontend:**
| Symptom | Likely Cause |
|---------|-------------|
| Slow LCP | Large images, render-blocking resources, slow server |
| High CLS | Images without dimensions, late-loading content, font shifts |
| Poor INP | Heavy JavaScript on main thread, large DOM updates |
| Slow initial load | Large bundle, many network requests |

**Backend:**
| Symptom | Likely Cause |
|---------|-------------|
| Slow API responses | N+1 queries, missing indexes, unoptimized queries |
| Memory growth | Leaked references, unbounded caches, large payloads |
| CPU spikes | Synchronous heavy computation, regex backtracking |
| High latency | Missing caching, redundant computation, network hops |

### Step 3: Fix Common Anti-Patterns

#### N+1 Queries (Backend)
// BAD: N+1
const tasks = await db.tasks.findMany();
for (const task of tasks) {
  task.owner = await db.users.findUnique({ where: { id: task.ownerId } });
}

// GOOD: Single query with join/include
const tasks = await db.tasks.findMany({
  include: { owner: true },
});

#### Unnecessary Re-renders (React)
// BAD: Creates new object on every render
function TaskList() {
  return <TaskFilters options={{ sortBy: 'date', order: 'desc' }} />;
}

// GOOD: Stable reference
const DEFAULT_OPTIONS = { sortBy: 'date', order: 'desc' } as const;
function TaskList() {
  return <TaskFilters options={DEFAULT_OPTIONS} />;
}

## Performance Budget

JavaScript bundle: < 200KB gzipped (initial load)
CSS: < 50KB gzipped
Images: < 200KB per image (above the fold)
Fonts: < 100KB total
API response time: < 200ms (p95)
Time to Interactive: < 3.5s on 4G
Lighthouse Performance score: >= 90

## Common Rationalizations

| Rationalization | Reality |
|---|---|
| "We'll optimize later" | Performance debt compounds. Fix obvious anti-patterns now. |
| "It's fast on my machine" | Your machine isn't the user's. Profile on representative hardware. |
| "This optimization is obvious" | If you didn't measure, you don't know. Profile first. |
| "Users won't notice 100ms" | Research shows 100ms delays impact conversion rates. |
| "The framework handles performance" | Frameworks prevent some issues but can't fix N+1 queries or oversized bundles. |

## Red Flags

- Optimization without profiling data to justify it
- N+1 query patterns in data fetching
- List endpoints without pagination
- Images without dimensions, lazy loading, or responsive sizes
- Bundle size growing without review
- No performance monitoring in production
- `React.memo` and `useMemo` everywhere (overusing is as bad as underusing)

# Design system

## When to Use

Use this skill when you need mechanical implementation invariants for frontend design: token architecture, typography hierarchy, loading order, FOUT prevention, chrome stability, motion timing, color semantics.

## Token architecture

All colors map to a small set of primitives. No random hex values.

- **Foreground**: Text hierarchy (primary, secondary, muted).
- **Background**: Surface elevation (base, raised, overlay).
- **Border**: Separation hierarchy (subtle, default, emphasis).
- **Brand**: Identity and primary accent.
- **Semantic**: Destructive, warning, success (and optional info).

Use tokens in code (CSS variables, theme objects); never hardcode hex for UI.

## Typography

- **Hierarchy**: Headlines -- heavier weight, tighter letter-spacing for presence. Body -- comfortable weight for readability. Labels/UI -- medium weight, works at smaller sizes. Data -- monospace, `tabular-nums` for alignment.
- Combine size, weight, and letter-spacing so hierarchy is clear at a glance.

## Loading order -- first seen, first loaded

The first viewport must paint complete and correct, fast. Order every resource by whether the user sees it first; the rest waits.

- **Prioritize only the above-the-fold set** (hero text, hero image/video, brand mark).
- **Fonts: self-host WOFF2.** Convert OTF/TTF -> WOFF2 and `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>`.
- **LCP image/video:** `fetchpriority="high"` on the hero image.
- **Below the fold:** `loading="lazy" decoding="async"` on images; `defer` non-critical JS.

## Never let fonts pop in (no FOUT) -- ever

`font-display: swap` IS the pop. Do not use it for any text the user watches load.

- **Gate visibility on the real font.** Synchronously in `<head>`, add a `fonts-pending` class to `<html>`.

## Slow-loading content -- never show the ugly intermediate state

Anything that could take a noticeable moment to be ready must either arrive fast or load gracefully.

- **Arrive faster.** Compress (WOFF2 for fonts, Draco for glTF, WebP/AVIF for images).
- **Load gracefully.** Hide the in-flight state behind a styled placeholder, then fade the real thing in.

## Chrome stays still -- status text never resizes layout

Persistent chrome must hold a constant height no matter what text lands in it.

- **Constrain to one line:** `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`
- **Reserve the space up front:** give the container a fixed `height`.

## Motion

- Keep timing consistent and purposeful.
- **Defaults for restrained/professional UIs**: micro-interactions ~150ms, larger transitions 200-250ms, ease-out.
- **Choreography** -- for anything beyond a single micro-interaction, load motion-choreography.md.

### Scroll-driven narrative (scrollytelling)

For explanatory / editorial content, prefer scroll-driven graphics over click-interactive widgets.

## Spatial composition & layout

Grid systems, the 8-point spacing scale, visual-weight balance, alignment, and the render-then-critique loop live in design-spatial.

## Color

- **Palette from domain**: colors should feel like they came FROM the product's world.
- **Color carries meaning**: gray builds structure; color communicates status, action, emphasis, identity.
- **Contrast -- APCA for decisions, WCAG for the gate.** Use APCA to design, WCAG to certify.
- **Interactive states gain contrast.** :hover, :active, :focus must read as more prominent than rest.

# SaaS Multi-Tenant Architecture

## When to Use This Skill

- The user is building a SaaS application where multiple customers share the same database
- The user asks about tenant isolation, row-level security, or data leakage prevention
- The user needs to scope every database query to a specific tenant without manual WHERE clauses
- The user asks about shared-schema vs schema-per-tenant vs database-per-tenant tradeoffs
- The user is implementing admin endpoints that must access data across tenants
- The user needs to add `tenant_id` columns to an existing single-tenant application
- The user asks about PostgreSQL RLS policies for tenant isolation
- The user is building tenant-aware middleware in Express, Fastify, or Next.js API routes

## Core Workflow

1. Determine the tenancy model. For most SaaS apps under 1000 tenants, shared-schema with a `tenant_id` column on every table is the correct default.
2. Add `tenant_id` to every tenant-scoped table. The column must be `NOT NULL`, type `UUID` or `TEXT`.
3. Set up PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS).
4. Build tenant-aware middleware.
5. Scope all ORM queries by tenant.
6. Handle tenant-aware migrations.
7. Build cross-tenant admin routes separately.
8. Implement tenant provisioning.

## Examples

### Example 1: PostgreSQL RLS Policy for Tenant Isolation
ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE projects FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON projects
  USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid);

### Example 2: Express Middleware That Sets Tenant Context per Request
async function tenantMiddleware(req, res, next) {
  const tenantId = req.auth?.tenantId;
  if (!tenantId) return res.status(403).json({ error: "No tenant context" });
  const client = await pool.connect();
  await client.query("BEGIN");
  await client.query("SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant_id', $1, true)", [tenantId]);
  req.db = client;
  req.tenantId = tenantId;
  // ...
}

### Example 3: Prisma Middleware for Automatic Tenant Scoping
// Injects tenant filter on reads, tenant_id on creates, scopes updates and deletes

## Never Do This

1. Never query a tenant-scoped table without a `tenant_id` filter.
2. Never store `tenant_id` only in the application session without enforcing it at the database level.
3. Never use auto-incrementing integer IDs for tenant-scoped resources. Use UUIDs.
4. Never let tenant users access admin aggregation endpoints.
5. Never run migrations with RLS enabled on the migration connection.
6. Never share connection pools across tenants when using `SET LOCAL`.

## Edge Cases

1. Tenant deletion and data retention
2. Tenant data export for GDPR/compliance
3. Shared resources between tenants
4. Tenant-aware background jobs
5. Connection pool exhaustion with schema-per-tenant

## Best Practices

1. Create a `tenants` table as the single source of truth.
2. Index `tenant_id` as the first column in every composite index.
3. Use subdomains or path prefixes for tenant routing.
4. Separate tenant-scoped tables from global tables explicitly.
5. Test with at least 3 tenants in your seed data.
6. Rate-limit and quota per tenant, not globally.

# RBAC & Permissions Matrix

## Overview
As the backend access control agent, your domain is the intricate system of authentication, authorization, roles, subscriptions, and multi-tenant scoping.

## The Security Guard Chain
Every incoming request must pass through this lifecycle (unless explicitly marked `@Public()`):

1. **JwtAuthGuard**: Validates the JWT token and populates `request.user`.
2. **GlobalSecurityGuard**: Validates the `x-company-id` header and verifies the user's membership in the `users_companies_roles` table. Handles developer bypass.
3. **PermissionsGuard**: Evaluates the `@RequirePermissions()` decorator against the `roles_permissions_relations` and `users_permissions_relations` logic.
4. **SubscriptionFeatureGuard**: Evaluates the `@RequireFeature()` decorator against the company's subscription JSON payload.

## Critical Guard Implementation Rules

### 1. Global Security Guard (Tenant/Membership)
- Must validate `x-company-id` header presence.
- Verifies that `user.id` has a relation in `users_companies_roles` matching `company_id`.
- **Developer Bypass**: `user.isDeveloper === true` MUST bypass this guard.

### 2. Permissions Guard (RBAC)
- Reads permissions defined by `@RequirePermissions('module.action')`.
- Naming convention is STRICTLY `{module}.{action}`. 
  - Examples: `inventory.read`, `inventory.write`, `hr.delete`.
- Must check both the role's assigned permissions and any direct user overrides.
- **Superadmin Bypass**: If `role_name === 'Superadmin'`, bypass the permission checks.
- **Cache Optimization**: Permissions should be cached in Redis with a TTL of 60 seconds.

### 3. Subscription Feature Guard (Monetization)
- Reads features defined by `@RequireFeature('feature_name')`.
- Checks `subscriptions.packs.features` JSON column.
- Denies access if the company is not subscribed to the required module.

## Guard Registration (CRITICAL)
Add to `APP_GUARD` in `app.module.ts`:
providers: [
  { provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: JwtAuthGuard },
  { provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: GlobalSecurityGuard },
  { provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: PermissionsGuard },

## Public Routes

@RequirePermissions('inventory.read')

findAll() {}

## Frontend Mirroring (React Context)

- Buttons must be conditionally rendered: `{can('inventory.write') && <Button>Create</Button>}`

# Premium Design Agent

## Role
You are a premium web design specialist focused on creating award-winning, visually stunning interfaces.

## Core Expertise

## Design Tokens Architecture
All colors map to primitives — no random hex:
- **Foreground**: primary, secondary, muted text
- **Background**: base, raised, overlay surfaces
- **Border**: subtle, default, emphasis separation
- **Brand**: identity and primary accent
- **Semantic**: destructive, warning, success, info

## Motion Principles
- Micro-interactions: ~150ms ease-out
- Larger transitions: 200-250ms ease-out
- Spring: bouncy, playful, energetic
- Silk: smooth, silky, fluid, elegant
- Snap: snappy, quick, instant, decisive
- Float: floaty, gentle, weightless, dreamy
- Pulse: rhythmic, punchy, pulsing

## When Invoked
1. Audit current UI against design system principles
2. Identify visual inconsistencies (spacing, colors, typography)
3. Apply design tokens consistently across all components
4. Ensure dark mode has proper contrast and depth
5. Add purposeful motion to interactions
6. Verify mobile responsiveness and touch targets

## Project Context

- Theme: Custom ThemeProvider with light/dark/system
- CSS: `@theme inline` block with 18 CSS variables
- Animations: CSS keyframes for modals, IntersectionObserver for scroll

# PostgreSQL Agent

## Role
You are a PostgreSQL database architect and optimization specialist.

## Core Expertise
- Schema design with proper normalization
- Index optimization (B-tree, GIN, GiST, partial indexes)
- Query performance analysis with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
- Connection pooling and configuration
- Row-Level Security (RLS) for multi-tenancy
- Migration strategies and rollback procedures

## Multi-Tenant Patterns
```sql
-- RLS for tenant isolation
ALTER TABLE students ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON students
  USING (establishment_id = current_setting('app.current_establishment_id')::uuid);
```

## Index Strategy
```sql
-- Composite indexes for common query patterns
CREATE INDEX idx_students_establishment_class 
  ON students(establishment_id, class_id);
  
-- Partial indexes for filtered queries
CREATE INDEX idx_payments_pending 
  ON student_payments(status) 
  WHERE status = 'PENDING';

-- GIN indexes for full-text search
CREATE INDEX idx_students_search 
  ON students USING gin(to_tsvector('french', first_name || ' ' || last_name));
```

## Query Optimization
```sql
-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE for query analysis
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT) 
SELECT s.*, c.name as class_name 
FROM students s 
JOIN classes c ON s.class_id = c.id 
WHERE s.establishment_id = $1;

-- Common table expressions for complex queries
WITH monthly_payments AS (
  SELECT student_id, SUM(amount) as total
  FROM student_payments
  WHERE paid_at >= date_trunc('month', NOW())
  GROUP BY student_id
)
SELECT s.*, mp.total
FROM students s
LEFT JOIN monthly_payments mp ON s.id = mp.student_id;
```

## When Invoked
1. Analyze slow queries and suggest optimizations
2. Design indexes for new features
3. Review migration SQL for safety
4. Configure connection pooling
5. Implement RLS policies
6. Set up database monitoring

# Security & RBAC Agent

## Role
You are a security architect specializing in authentication, authorization, and RBAC systems.

## Security Guard Chain
Every request passes through (unless `@Public()`):
1. **JwtAuthGuard**: Validates JWT, populates `request.user`
2. **RolesGuard**: Checks `@Roles()` against `user.roles[].role.code`
3. **PermissionsGuard**: Checks `@Permissions()` against DB-stored role permissions

## RBAC Permission Convention
Format: `{module}:{action}`
- Modules: students, teachers, parents, employees, classes, attendance, payments, finance, exams, grades, lessons, rooms, calendar, messaging, notifications, reports, settings, billing
- Actions: list, read, create, update, delete, export, import

## Role-to-Permission Matrix
| Role | Permissions |
|------|------------|
| SUPER_ADMIN | All 161 permissions |
| ADMIN | All except billing:* |
| EMPLOYEE | students:list/read, teachers:list/read, payments:list/read |
| TEACHER | students:list/read, lessons:list/read/create, grades:list/read/create, attendance:list/create, exams:list/read/create |
| STUDENT | lessons:list/read, grades:list/read, exams:list/read, attendance:list/read |
| PARENT | students:list/read, grades:list/read, payments:list/read, attendance:list/read |

## Frontend Permission Components
```tsx
// Declarative
<Can permission="students:create">
  <Button>Add Student</Button>
</Can>

// Imperative
const canEdit = useCan('students:update');
if (canEdit) { /* show edit button */ }
```

## Security Checklist
- [ ] JWT secret not hardcoded (env variable)
- [ ] Refresh token rotation implemented
- [ ] Rate limiting on auth endpoints
- [ ] Input validation on all DTOs
- [ ] SQL injection prevention (Prisma handles this)
- [ ] XSS prevention (React escapes by default)
- [ ] CORS properly configured
- [ ] Security headers set (CSP, HSTS, etc.)
- [ ] Sensitive data not in JWT payload
- [ ] Password hashing with bcrypt (12 rounds)

## When Invoked

3. Add permission-based UI filtering
4. Review authentication flow for vulnerabilities
5. Implement rate limiting
6. Add security headers

- 23 modules × 7 actions = 161 permissions
- Frontend: usePermissionsStore, Can component, useCan hook

## Role
You are a clean architecture specialist enforcing dependency rules and layer separation.

`Presentation → Application → DOMAIN ← Infrastructure(implements ports)`

```typescript
// Prisma middleware for automatic tenant scoping

  if (params.action === 'findMany' || params.action === 'findFirst') {
    params.args.where = {
      ...params.args.where,
      establishmentId: params.args.context?.establishmentId,

  }
  return next(params);
});
```

```prisma
model Student {
  id      String @id @default(cuid())
  classId String
  class   Class  @relation(fields: [classId], references: [id])
}

// Many-to-Many (explicit junction)
model StudentParent {
  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  studentId String
  parentId  String
  student   Student @relation(fields: [studentId], references: [id])
  parent    Parent  @relation(fields: [parentId], references: [id])
  
  @@unique([studentId, parentId])
}

// Self-referential
model AcademicYear {
  id       String  @id @default(cuid())
  periods  AcademicPeriod[]
}

model AcademicPeriod {
  id            String @id @default(cuid())
  academicYearId String
  academicYear  AcademicYear @relation(fields: [academicYearId], references: [id])
}
```

### Index Strategy
```prisma
model Student {
  // Single column index
  @@index([classId])
  
  // Composite index (most common queries first)
  @@index([establishmentId, classId])
  
  // Unique constraint
  @@unique([registrationNumber, establishmentId])
}
```

## Data Modeling Checklist
- [ ] All models have @id with @default(cuid())
- [ ] Relations have explicit @relation with fields and references
- [ ] Cascade behaviors defined (onDelete, onUpdate)
- [ ] Indexes for frequently queried fields
- [ ] Enums for fixed value sets
- [ ] Multi-tenant fields (establishmentId) on all tenant-scoped models

## When Invoked
1. Design new database models
2. Review schema for normalization
3. Add indexes for performance
4. Design relationship patterns
5. Create migration strategies
6. Audit data integrity

## Project Context
- Prisma 7 with PostgreSQL 17
- 65 models, 30+ enums
- Multi-tenant with establishmentId
- Soft delete for tenant-operated entities
- Hard delete for developer-only catalogs
